definition: To do physical exercise, usually at a gym.
business_context_example: I work out three times a week before the office opens.

definition: To do gentle exercise before training to prepare the body.
business_context_example: Always warm up for 10 minutes or you'll pull something.

definition: To do gentle exercise after training so the body recovers.
business_context_example: We cool down with stretching and a slow walk.

definition: To become physically fit.
business_context_example: I joined the gym in January to get in shape before the summer.

definition: Not physically fit.
business_context_example: After two years at a desk I'm completely out of shape.

definition: To make your muscles bigger and stronger through training.
business_context_example: You need protein and rest to build muscle, not just heavy weights.

definition: To train with heavy objects to get stronger.
business_context_example: She lifts weights on Mondays and runs on Thursdays.

definition: Repetitions: how many times you repeat an exercise in one set.
business_context_example: Do 12 reps, rest 60 seconds, then repeat three times.

definition: Your own best ever result in a sport.
business_context_example: He ran a personal best of 42 minutes in the 10K.

definition: A professional who plans and guides your training.
business_context_example: A personal trainer fixed my technique in two sessions.

definition: The ability to keep going physically for a long time.
business_context_example: Cycling to work built up my endurance without any extra time.

definition: Physical or mental energy that lets you keep going.
business_context_example: Long meetings need the same stamina as a long run, honestly.

definition: To start doing a sport regularly.
business_context_example: I took up swimming after my back started hurting.

definition: To stop doing something you used to do.
business_context_example: He gave up football at 35 and switched to tennis.

definition: To stay healthy through regular exercise.
business_context_example: Walking the dog twice a day is how I keep fit.

definition: To practise with a lot of effort.
business_context_example: They trained hard all winter and it showed in the first match.

definition: A person who trains a team or athlete; also, to train someone.
business_context_example: The new coach changed the whole style of the team.

definition: The full group of players available for a team.
business_context_example: Only 11 start, but the squad has 22 players.

definition: The list of players chosen to start a game.
business_context_example: The line-up was announced an hour before kick-off.

definition: The start of a football match.
business_context_example: Kick-off is at 8, so let's meet at half past seven.

definition: The break in the middle of a match.
business_context_example: They were losing 2-0 at half-time and still won.

definition: Additional playing time when the score is level.
business_context_example: The final went to extra time and then penalties.

definition: A result where both teams have the same score.
business_context_example: A 1-1 draw was a fair result for both sides.

definition: To defeat someone in a game or competition.
business_context_example: We beat them 3-0 away, which nobody expected.

definition: To beat someone very easily by a big score.
business_context_example: They thrashed us 6-1 and we deserved it.

definition: A victory by a very small margin.
business_context_example: It was a narrow win, 1-0 with a goal in the last minute.

definition: The person or team that finishes second.
business_context_example: She was runner-up in the national championship two years running.

definition: The player or team expected to lose.
business_context_example: Everyone loves an underdog, especially when they win.

definition: The benefit of playing in your own stadium with your own fans.
business_context_example: Home advantage is worth a goal in a game like this.

definition: A match played at the opponent's ground.
business_context_example: The away game in Varna is on Saturday.

definition: A scheduled sports match.
business_context_example: The fixture was moved to Sunday because of the weather.

definition: The official who controls a match and applies the rules.
business_context_example: The referee gave a penalty that nobody in the stadium understood.

definition: An action against the rules of the game.
business_context_example: It was a clear foul, but play continued.

definition: Ordered to leave the field as a punishment.
business_context_example: Their captain was sent off in the first half.

definition: To get a point or goal; also, the record of points.
business_context_example: He scored twice in ten minutes.

definition: To score and make the scores level.
business_context_example: They equalised in the 89th minute and the stadium went quiet.

definition: A practice game played before an important competition.
business_context_example: The warm-up match showed the defence still isn't ready.

definition: To injure a muscle by stretching it too far.
business_context_example: I pulled a muscle sprinting for the bus, of all things.

definition: To injure a joint by twisting it.
business_context_example: She sprained her ankle in training and missed three weeks.

definition: To be unable to play because of an injury.
business_context_example: Their best striker is out injured until October.
translation_bg: да съм извън игра заради контузия

definition: To get better after illness or injury.
business_context_example: He recovered faster than expected and played on Sunday.

definition: To become exhausted from training or working too hard.
business_context_example: Young players burn out when nobody tells them to rest.

definition: A planned day without training.
business_context_example: Sunday is a rest day, and it's part of the plan, not a break from it.

definition: To be a fan of a particular team.
business_context_example: I've supported the same team since I was six.

definition: A fan of a team.
business_context_example: Two thousand supporters travelled to the away game.

definition: A ticket that covers all home matches in a season.
business_context_example: A season ticket works out cheaper than eight single games.

definition: To watch a match, usually on TV.
business_context_example: Did you catch the game last night?

definition: A short video showing the best moments of a match.
business_context_example: I missed it live, so I watched the highlights on the train.

definition: The ranking of teams in a competition.
business_context_example: Three wins moved them to second in the league table.

definition: A situation where everyone has an equal chance.
business_context_example: Online lessons gave smaller schools a level playing field.
